name: Mark DeSaulnier

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE
statements.title: AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE
sentences: As Democrats, we stand for quality, affordability, and universal health coverage.
I was involved in California's adaptation to the Affordable Care Act's success, and I also come as a small business owner.

Mr. Speaker, it has been a pleasure to work with the chairman on so many issues that affect American working families where they continue to get crushed by inflation and higher costs to all their household demands, particularly healthcare.

All of that money that they have to spend goes to the wealthiest amongst us, to further one of the greatest transfers of wealth in the history of this country to people who already have obscene amounts of money.
Last year, Congressional Republicans and the President passed the big ugly bill, which cuts around $1 trillion from Medicaid over 10 years.
Republicans also failed, as Mr. Scott explained, to extend the enhanced premium tax credit that helped millions more Americans as we got through COVID and found out it worked.
In my county where I was a county supervisor, they will have to take it out of police services and the library and other public services.
It goes to the wealthiest Americans in this country.
In my district, which is the fifth wealthiest House district out of 435 in the United States, I have a private hospital system that used to be about 95 percent private pay.
They are now almost 50 percent Medi- Cal/Medicaid.
This is in the fifth wealthiest district in the United States with lots of challenges and diversity to stay in business.
In addition, $3 million on the ACA marketplace cuts and failing to extend PTC, and as I said, the ripple effect on everything else in the private sector and in the local economy.
These policies also put a strain on our healthcare system, as I have mentioned, that impact patients beyond those on Medicaid.
An analysis by Public Citizen found that 446 hospitals are at heightened risk of closing due to the Medicaid cuts.

The publicly owned hospital of which, many years ago when I was a Republican on a 5-member county board of supervisors, I was the deciding vote to rebuild it 25 years ago--that publicly owned hospital in the clinic system I represent is facing a 5-year cumulative deficit of around $890 million, due almost entirely to the big, ugly bill, and State-level changes that the State is required to do which are now requiring the local governments to do.
I hate to repeat myself, but it went to the top 1 percent.
This money that we are giving the wealthiest Americans--the obscenely wealthy Americans from this bill--will make that worse.
I will always remember these words because everyone who has ever been diagnosed with cancer remembers when they were diagnosed.
We spend 18 percent of our GDP on healthcare, but of all developed countries, which I will going into in more detail, we get the worst outcomes.

We will lose 51,000 Americans just in 2027, according to this nonpartisan investigation by the University of Pennsylvania that is corroborated by multiple other nonprofit/nonpartisan foundations and research think tanks.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: E-CIGARETTES ADDICT YOUNG PEOPLE
statements.title: E-CIGARETTES ADDICT YOUNG PEOPLE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to express my outrage about recent FDA regulatory actions on e-cigarettes.
On April 30, Reynolds American donated $5 million to MAGA Inc., a Trump-backed super-PAC.
In the following 8 days, the President dined with top tobacco executives, and the FDA issued guidance making it easier for tobacco companies to sell flavored e-cigarettes.
In 2024, 1.63 million middle and high school students in America used e-cigarettes, and nearly 90 percent of them used flavored products.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to join me in condemning this blatant, pay-for-play corruption and the harm it will inflict to generations of young Americans. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESTORING ELECTION INTEGRITY
statements.title: RESTORING ELECTION INTEGRITY
sentences: This is such an important discussion for Americans, and I think most Americans don't realize what a deliberate effort this was for years to take away their power and place it in the hands of the wealthiest and, unfortunately, the most obscenely greedy people in this country who think only they have the wisdom to govern.

I thank the gentleman for giving me the opportunity to highlight how Citizens United has impacted not just the political landscape and indeed this room but also our Nation, our culture, and certainly our economy.
With the floodgates opened by the Supreme Court in 2010, corporations and billionaires can now make unlimited independent expenditures.
According to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, the 2017 Trump tax cuts overwhelmingly favored the rich.

The lowest 20 percent of earners got an average tax break of only $70 while the top 1 percent of earners received over $61,000 in tax breaks, and the top tenth of a percent saw over $250,000 of tax breaks.

Those same tax cuts lowered the corporate tax rate from 35 percent to 21 percent, which the Bipartisan Policy Center projected will increase the Federal deficit by almost $1 trillion dollars by fiscal year 2027.

Unsurprisingly, during the same period, billionaire spending on Presidential elections has skyrocketed, increasing from a total of $16 million before Citizens United was passed to over $2.6 billion in the years since Citizens United.

When billionaires and corporations are able to spend unlimited amounts to influence the results of our elections, our elected officials are, in turn, unfortunately, more likely to respond by passing legislation that benefits corporations and the richest Americans while making life more expensive for middle-class Americans.
Our Nation and the world are experiencing record levels of income inequality, and the impacts of Citizens United and other handouts to the obscenely rich and powerful are only making it worse.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS EVERYONE
statements.title: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS EVERYONE
sentences: When everyone is cut off from Medicaid, where will they go?
There are 78.5 million people enrolled in Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program across America.
One in three people with disabilities, 15 million, have Medicaid.
Comparatively, 19 percent of adults without disabilities have Medicaid.
One in five Medicaid enrollees has a disability.
Two-thirds of Medicaid enrollees do not receive SSI benefits.
Mr. Speaker, 10.3 million people would lose Medicaid coverage in the next 10 years if the budget reconciliation bill of the Republicans passes because of its punitive work requirements.
In 2022, Medicaid covered two-thirds of all home-care spending. 4.5 million people receive Medicaid-covered home-care services each year in America.

Medicaid cuts as proposed under the Republican budget threaten optional benefits the most, including long-term services and supports that help the disabled and the elderly in home- and community-based services that help protect these Americans who need our help.
In California alone, almost 15 million Californians are on Medicaid. 1,906,300 Californians on Medicaid have a disability.

A million people in California with disabilities who get Medicaid are working, and now they are going to be forced to go through a bureaucracy that supposedly the majority wants to make more efficient.
Mr. Speaker, 68 percent of California adults on Medicaid have a job.

In just my district, which is the fifth wealthiest district in the House, 131,634 people are on Medicaid and are at risk of losing care under the Republican budget. 45,916 of those are children, 19,000 are seniors, 10,000 are people with disabilities, 48,300 adults are on Medicaid due to ACA expansion.

statements.title: RISING COSTS FOR SMALL BUSINESSES

Mr. Speaker, recent surveys have said, 42 percent of small businesses reported increased costs due to the administration's policies, both tariffs and otherwise.

statements.title: DEFUNDING SUICIDE HOTLINE FOR LGBTQ YOUTH

In recognition of these challenges, the challenges these Americans face, the 988 lifeline provides specialty services targeted at LGBTQ youth, who are at a higher risk of suicide than the population at large.
According to a 2024 survey by the Trevor Project, 12 percent of LGBTQ youth attempted suicide in the past year--12 percent of American youth in this category.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.J. RES. 60, PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE NATIONAL PARK SERVICE RELATING TO "GLEN CANYON NAT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.J. RES. 60, PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE NATIONAL PARK SERVICE RELATING TO "GLEN CANYON NATIONAL RECREATION AREA: MOTOR...
sentences: Under the U.S. Clean Air Act, signed by President Richard Nixon, we did that, and we have been leaders since he signed it.

Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to specifically three Congressional Review Act resolutions that are in this rule that illegally take aim at California's legal ability to implement more stringent emission standards under waiver from the Clean Air Act.
In the last 2 months, the Senate Parliamentarian and the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office affirmed that California's Clean Air Act waiver is not subject to the Congressional Review Act.
On top of that, these CRAs are another unfounded attempt to limit States from having the choice to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve air quality and their public health.
States can choose to join California under the Clean Air Act.

I proudly served on the California Air Resources Board under three Governors, including two Republicans and one Democrat, and I have seen firsthand the benefits of curbing emissions, both for the economy and public health.
Republican Governor Ronald Reagan signed into law the creation of the California State Air Resources Board and Republican President Richard Nixon signed into law the California Clean Air Act.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to this rule and the resolutions it advances.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PRESIDENT TRUMP'S CLEMENCY GRANTS
statements.title: PRESIDENT TRUMP'S CLEMENCY GRANTS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, immediately after taking office, the current President granted sweeping pardons and commutations to over 1,500 insurrectionists who stormed the Capitol on January 6, 2021.
At least 174 police officers were injured while protecting the Capitol that day, and 5 officers who responded later died.
I was one of the last Members who was evacuated from this building on January 6.
I have vivid memories, as many of us do, of the Capitol Police officers battered and exhausted but still defending us.
The decision to grant clemency to many violent and dangerous individuals is an affront to our democracy, our justice system, and the brave police officers who defended us that day and every day.
